rounds.text: TBZ carries significant leverage risk as its debt-to-equity ratio has reached 1.06x, meaning total debt now exceeds the company's net worth [E38]. This financial strain is exacerbated by poor earnings quality, shown by a cash conversion ratio of only 0.15x for March 2026, which indicates that reported profits are not being realized as cash [E34]. Total borrowings have climbed to Rs 886 Cr [E40], while operating cash flow remains a meager 27% of operating profit [E37]. Although recent performance is high, the company’s median return on equity over a ten-year period is just 9% [E26], and the stock has a history of extreme volatility with a record drawdown of -93.4% [E54]. The business also exhibits inconsistent trends in both yearly and quarterly operating margins [E32, E33], while recent data shows that earnings growth is decelerating [E67]. Conceded: TBZ currently trades at a low P/E of 7.86x [E1] and has achieved a massive 189% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21]. However, the annualized volatility of 53.7% and a cyclical earnings profile indicate significant instability [E55, E59].
